title: Scam Texts and Calls
about: Spot the signs of a scam text or call before you reply.

cards.prompt: You're expecting a parcel. **Tap** each part.

parts.job: A small fee. Real deliveries don't text you to pay a few dollars at a link.
A deadline. "Within 2 hours" rushes you so you don't stop to think.
A strange link. parcels-redelivery.example isn't the real Parcels app or website.

cards.explanation: A scam text often wants a **small fee**, sets a **deadline** and adds a **link**.

cards.sentence: Never tap a link in a surprise text: open the company's **own app** to check.

cards.prompt: Tap the **three** scam signs in the new text.
cards.explanation: It wants a **small fee**, sets a **deadline** and adds a **link** to `parcels-redelivery.example`. The sender name is faked to blend in.
cards.hint: Find what it wants you to pay, how long it gives you, and where it sends you.
cards.nudge: Look for a fee, a deadline and a link in the new message, one at a time.

cards.prompt: A call sounds just like your cousin: a [[voice clone|voice-clone]].

steps.text: **"Send $200 in gift cards now. Tell no one!"** What now?

choices.consequence: Voices can be copied, and gift cards are a scammer's favourite. The money would be gone.

choices.text: Keep it secret, like they asked
choices.consequence: Secrecy is a warning sign. It stops anyone helping you check.

choices.text: Hang up, call their saved number
choices.consequence: Your cousin answers, confused and fine. It was a scam, and you stopped it.

cards.explanation: A familiar voice can be faked. **Hang up and call back** on a number you already have.
cards.hint: How can you reach your cousin in a way a scammer can't fake?

cards.title: Scam calls
cards.body:
A scam caller may say they're your bank or the police. **Hang up** if they want a **code**, a **password**, **gift cards**, **secrecy** or **control of your computer**.

Then **call back** on a number you already have, like the one on your card.

items.label: Caller asks for the code texted to you
"Pay in gift cards or be arrested"
You call the number on the bank's site
You call a friend on their saved number

cards.explanation: Codes, controlling your computer, gift cards and secrecy are scam signs: **hang up**. Calling a number you found yourself is fine.
cards.hint: Check each against the warning signs for calls, and ask who chose the number.
cards.nudge: Look at each one again: does it match a warning sign, and who chose the number?

options.text: Being asked to pay a fee in gift cards to claim a prize
A text from a number that isn't saved in your phone
options.nudge: New numbers can be fine: the dentist, a new classmate.

options.text: A receipt email for an order you placed this morning
options.nudge: A receipt for something you really bought is normal.

cards.explanation: Real prizes never cost money to claim, and gift cards are a favourite scam payment. A new number or a real receipt can be normal.
cards.hint: What does a real prize cost to claim, and which payment were you told to hang up on?

cards.prompt: A text arrives from a number you don't know.

steps.text: **"It's your boss, new number. Buy three $100 gift cards and text me the codes. Keep it quiet!"** What do you do?

choices.consequence: Gift cards, rushing and secrecy are all scam signs. Once you send the codes, the money is gone.
The reply goes to the scammer, who will happily say yes.
Your boss has no idea what you mean. Scam stopped, and your boss warns the team.

cards.explanation: Check a "new number" text on a number you already have. Gift cards and secrecy are warning signs.
cards.hint: How can you reach your boss in a way a scammer can't fake?

cards.title: Recap
cards.body:
- A text with a **fee**, a **deadline** and a **link**? Check in the company's **official app**.
- A pushy call? **Hang up and call back** on a number you know.
- **Try this:** save your bank's real number in your contacts.

**Next:** a fake website that looks exactly like the real one.
